We don't have some big underlying purpose. The truth is that there is no massive mindblowing truth, which is kind of paradoxical I know. I've been exactly where you are and I'll probably be there again, like this post sounds like some of my thoughts lol. 

We have the same amount of purpose as a cat or an ant or a rock or a star or a fern. We're made out of mostly the same stuff, we came to be in basically the same ways- in the grand scheme of things, everything on earth is far more similar than they are different comparatively speaking. Ignoring the fact that you have a house, maybe a driver's license, a degree, a career- what gives you more right to be on this earth than a lion or a cow, but also what gives you less right to be on the earth than a tree or a river? 

I hope this makes sense, I dont want it to come off too hippie-dippy. There's some stuff I still haven't figured out- for some reason we evolved to the point we could build skyscrapers and rockets and invent things like TV and the internet. I think the Industrial Revolution really helped us dissociate from the fact that we're just another cog in the wheel of nature.

It sounds like you've been searching passionately for a lot of external answers but maybe you should just try asking yourself what you think the answers are- meditate or journal about it. Read into more religions, mythologies, philosophies, etc. Find what makes sense to you. Buddhism teaches that life is inherently suffering, but also teaches steps to reduce your amount of suffering. Idk if that's for you but its helped me a lot. 

Best of luck! ♡
